title: Check yourself: Success criteria and test sets

questions.stem: A team's goal reads "the extraction model should work well". Which rewrite meets the documentation's four traits of a good criterion?

options.text: Reach 100 percent accuracy on every field, so that no invoice needs a manual check
options.says: Ruled out because a target fails the Achievable trait when "The target is beyond what current frontier models can do", and perfect accuracy on every field is such a target.

options.text: Lift field-level F1 above 0.9 on the 40 invoices used to write the prompt
options.says: Ruled out because it scores the model on the cases the prompt was written from, and trap 3 says "Keep cases the prompt has never been shaped by".

options.text: Improve extraction until reviewers feel the output is clearly better
options.says: Ruled out because a feeling has no number, while a criterion must "Use quantitative metrics or well-defined qualitative scales".

options.text: Lift field-level F1 above 0.9 on 500 held-out invoices, beating today's 0.86
options.says: It names a metric (F1), a threshold above the current baseline, and a data set the model was not tuned on, which are the parts of the page's good example: "a held-out test set* of 10,000 diverse Twitter posts (Relevant), which is a 5% improvement over the current baseline (Achievable)".

origin.section: Four traits of a good criterion

questions.stem: A support bot's eval set contains 40 polite, well-formed questions. Production shows empty messages, pasted logs and abusive input. What is the best change to the set?

options.text: Add tagged cases for those awkward situations, sampled from live traffic
options.says: The first principle is to "Design evals that mirror your real-world task distribution", and its list of edge cases includes "poor, harmful or irrelevant user input" for chat use cases, and a set of polite questions has none.

options.text: Replace the questions with a smaller group graded by hand
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "More questions with slightly lower signal automated grading is better than fewer questions with high-quality human hand-graded evals".

options.text: Keep the set unchanged and raise the passing threshold
options.says: Ruled out because a stricter threshold on the same easy cases still measures a different task and, in the page's words, "Don't forget to factor in edge cases!".

options.text: Ask the model to write more polite questions of the same kind
options.says: Ruled out because the course's advice is to "Write the awkward inputs by hand", and more polite questions add none.

origin.section: A test set that mirrors the task

questions.stem: A prompt is refined for a week against a fixed set of 200 examples, and the pass rate climbs from 71 to 96 percent. The launch review wants to know whether 96 percent will hold on new traffic. Which evidence answers that?

options.text: The same fixed set rerun with a stricter grader
options.says: Ruled out because a stricter grader on the same set still scores the cases the prompt was shaped by, and the trap says "Keep cases the prompt has never been shaped by".

options.text: A longer list of the prompt changes made during the week
options.says: Ruled out because a list of changes records effort and carries no score, while the page asks for "Some ways to empirically test against those criteria".

options.text: A fresh slice of cases that played no part in any tuning
options.says: The page's example speaks of a "held-out test set", which is "data you did not tune on", and only that can say how the prompt will do on new input.

options.text: The pass rate on the same set averaged over five runs
options.says: Ruled out because repeating the tuned set only averages out noise, and the trap says "The score is then a memory test".

origin.section: Four traits of a good criterion
